PAPERS.title: Prenatal exposure to ultrafine particles and positive screening for postpartum depression: a prospective pregnancy cohort in Shanghai, China
PAPERS.pm: Residential trimester-specific UFP number and PM2.5 (modelled)
PAPERS.n: 2,647 pregnant women, two centres; 20.4% screened positive at 6-10 weeks postpartum. Per IQR, first-trimester UFP OR 1.252 (1.065-1.471) and whole-pregnancy UFP OR 1.104 (1.047-1.164); both survived adjustment for PM2.5, which had no stable independent association. Stronger with male infants. Limitation: EPDS is a screen, not a diagnosis, and the UFP surface's spatial resolution and validation are not stated - UFP gradients decay over ~100-300 m from roads, so residential misclassification is likely large and non-differential only if traffic proximity is unrelated to deprivation, which in Shanghai it is not. Relevance: high - a second UFP-specific neuro signal this month that PM2.5 mass does not carry, and that optical nodes cannot measure.

PAPERS.title: Extreme, Accumulated, and Lagged Exposure to Fire-Sourced PM2.5 and Site-specific Cancer Risk in China
PAPERS.pm: Fire-sourced vs all-source PM2.5; lagged, accumulated and extreme metrics
PAPERS.n: Fire-sourced PM2.5 was positively associated with several site-specific cancers, with lagged and accumulated metrics showing the broadest pattern (thyroid, kidney, breast, lung, leukaemia, lymphoma) and extreme exposure the narrowest (strongest for larynx). Against all-source PM2.5, fire PM2.5 associations were stronger for thyroid, kidney, larynx, lymphoma and oral cancers, and stronger in the north and in low-GDP areas. Limitation: no effect sizes, n or geographic unit in the abstract; many sites x three metrics is a multiple-comparison surface, and thyroid cancer incidence is notoriously driven by screening intensity, which tracks region and income. Relevance: moderate - source-resolved smoke again outperforms mass.

PAPERS.title: Forecasting transboundary PM10 pollution in northern Taiwan using upwind observations and transport timing
PAPERS.pm: PM10 at 3 receptors; 9 continental upwind records; trajectory timing composite
PAPERS.n: Upwind-transition-receptor framework with temporally separated training and evaluation for 1-4-day PM10 forecasts. Nested models attribute most added skill to distributed upwind observations; trajectory timing adds a smaller, receptor-dependent refinement. Best model (CatBoost with upwind data): RMSE 11.04 ug/m3, 13.0% below persistence. Limitation: 13% over persistence at 1-4 days is modest, and upper-tail precision is limited by event scarcity - the episodes that matter are the ones the model sees least. Relevance: high - quantitative evidence that upwind observation density, not trajectory sophistication, buys forecast skill; a siting argument for upwind nodes.

PAPERS.title: Biomass burning drives urban PM2.5 across the Western Balkans: evidence from a six-city source apportionment study in North Macedonia
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 from 1,195 daily filters, EPA PMF 5.0
PAPERS.n: 1,195 filters at six urban-background sites over two year-long campaigns. Campaign means 29.1-62.2 ug/m3 (1.2-2.5x the EU annual limit); residential wood combustion and open/waste burning resolved as distinct factors everywhere, together 21-35% of PM2.5, with heating-season RWC up to 33x non-heating. Biomass exceeded 50% of PM2.5 on 83% of Skopje episode days; an undocumented winter signal in Strumica fits greenhouse boilers. Limitation: PMF factor naming relies on tracer interpretation, and RWC/OBB separation without levoglucosan isotopes or 14C is assumption-laden. Relevance: high - a wood-smoke regime with bimodal evening peaks to 93 ug/m3, where optical sensor response to fresh smoke is the calibration problem.

PAPERS.title: Compound fire-meteorology extremes drove megacity air pollution during the 2024 South American fire season
PAPERS.pm: Surface PM2.5 and CO, AOT, trajectories; fire-on/fire-off global simulations
PAPERS.n: Three multi-day 2024 episodes with daily PM2.5 of 80-100 ug/m3 in metropolitan Sao Paulo. Fire-off simulations missed the PM2.5 and CO peaks; fire-attributable increments reached 17-21 ug/m3 state-wide and a cumulative metropolitan burden of ~547 ug/m3-day. Episodes differed in transport configuration, and the worst coincided with heat, dryness and weak ventilation. Limitation: all fire inventories underestimated the most extreme episode, so the attribution is a lower bound with unquantified error; a global model is coarse for a megacity receptor. Relevance: moderate - the inventory shortfall at the extreme is exactly where a dense surface network constrains attribution.

PAPERS.title: New operational perspective to identify aerosols and hydrometeors in real-time with a pioneering algorithm (CONIOPOL) based on single-wavelength polarization lidar (CL61)
PAPERS.pm: Volume depolarisation ratio and attenuated backscatter (Vaisala CL61 ceilometer)
PAPERS.n: Automated classification from a polarised automatic lidar-ceilometer combining depolarisation, attenuated backscatter and cloud base to separate aerosol, cloud phase and precipitation and to type aerosol as dust, smoke/marine, continental or mixed. One year at Uccle showed strong temporal and vertical correspondence with CAMS for transported dust and smoke. Limitation: single wavelength cannot separate smoke from marine aerosol, and validation against CAMS is model-conditioned agreement rather than in-situ truth. Relevance: high - ceilometers are already networked across Europe; vertical typing tells a surface sensor network when its column assumption is broken.

PAPERS.title: Asymptotic behavior of lidar scattering properties of absorbing dust aerosols across Rayleigh and geometrical-optics regimes: theory and implications
PAPERS.pm: Lidar ratio, depolarisation ratio, SSA vs size parameter and iron-oxide fraction
PAPERS.n: TAMUdust2020 and triaxial-ellipsoid calculations give shape-insensitive limits: Rayleigh S ~ x^-3, SSA ~ x^3, small depolarisation; geometric-optics depolarisation falls, SSA -> 1/2 and lidar ratio rises with strong absorption. Large, strongly absorbing dust can therefore mimic weakly depolarising classes and bias classifiers toward under-counting coarse and super-coarse dust. Limitation: theory only, no field test. Relevance: moderate - the same physics explains why optical PM sensors under-read coarse absorbing dust; the bias direction carries over.

PAPERS.title: Influence of irradiance and mixing layer height on the vertical trace matter distribution in the lower planetary boundary layer - drone-based investigation
PAPERS.pm: Drone vertical profiles of particle mass and number, CO2, O3 to 500 m
PAPERS.n: Two 2.5-week summer campaigns: night profiles in the lowest 120 m showed multi-layer fine-scale stratification; O3 and potential temperature were the most reliable mixing-height markers, and trace species outperformed several meteorological variables. Local sources and sinks affected in-layer distribution more than irradiance, but aerosol concentrations homogenised under strong radiation even at low mixing heights. Limitation: rural summer only; drone-borne particle sensors are themselves low-cost optical units with flow and RH artefacts that the abstract does not address. Relevance: high - directly tests when a ground node represents the mixed layer.

PAPERS.title: Size-Dependent Characteristics, Exposure Risk, and Formation Mechanisms of Environmentally Persistent Free Radicals in Atmospheric Particulate Matter
PAPERS.pm: EPFRs (EPR) in PM2.5, PM10, TSP; SiO2-catechol-ZnO simulations
PAPERS.n: EPFRs were carbon-centred radicals adjacent to oxygen groups; PM2.5 had the highest mass-normalised concentration (8.05e16 spins/g) and g-factor (2.00337). Cigarette-equivalent exposure was 0.326/day for PM2.5 and 0.346/day for PM10. Laboratory surrogates showed smaller particles generate more EPFRs owing to larger specific surface. Limitation: the cigarette-equivalent model is a communication device without dosimetric basis, and site/season details are absent from the abstract. Relevance: low-moderate - another surface-chemistry toxicity axis that mass sensing cannot see.

PAPERS.title: Exposure to environmental toxicants during pregnancy and placental angiogenic biomarkers: An integrative review
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5, PM10, NO2, O3 among other toxicants
PAPERS.n: Whittemore-Knafl integrative review: 19 human studies after screening. Air pollutants predominantly showed an anti-angiogenic pattern - higher sFlt-1 or sFlt-1/PlGF and lower PlGF - as did PFAS, Cd and Cu; 14 of 19 studies reported at least one association in that direction. Limitation: 19 heterogeneous studies across four toxicant classes, no pooling or bias assessment, and 'at least one association' across multiple biomarkers and windows is a low bar. Relevance: low-moderate - plausible mechanism for PM-preeclampsia links, not evidence of it.

PAPERS.title: Public health guidance about wildfire smoke: Four targets for improvement
PAPERS.n: Commentary proposing four distinct targets for improving Canadian wildfire-smoke guidance: a stronger evidence base (subpopulations, long-term effects, protective interventions), ethically deliberated recommendations, evaluation of guidance effectiveness beyond self-report, and a process-and-content standard for authoritative guidance. Limitation: no data. Relevance: moderate - the evaluation target presupposes measured indoor and personal exposure during smoke events, which is where low-cost sensors already dominate the evidence.

PAPERS.title: Divergent bacterial signatures in dental clinic bioaerosols: a real-field investigation
PAPERS.pm: Optical particle sizer; Andersen six-stage culturable and filter bioaerosol sampling
PAPERS.endpoint: Airborne and surface bacterial load and community
PAPERS.n: Ultrasonic scaling caused a large surge in sub-micron particle counts, but culturable bacteria concentrated in the 1.1-3.3 um stages. Airborne bacterial communities differed from PPE (ANOSIM R=0.633, p=0.001) and were indistinguishable from non-touch surfaces; oral pathogens were rare in air. Limitation: single clinic and procedure type, small sample count not given. Relevance: moderate - a clean demonstration that particle number from an optical counter is not a proxy for biological load; mirrors the 4 Oct suction study.

PAPERS.title: Spatio-Temporal Trends in Wildfire Smoke Exposures at Schools and Childcare Centers in the United States and Implications for Child and Adolescent Health
PAPERS.pm: Wildfire smoke PM2.5 at school and childcare locations
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates national spatiotemporal trends in smoke exposure at schools and childcare centres. Recorded for coverage; no estimate inferred. Relevance: high if the exposure surface is sensor-informed - school sensor deployments are the most common LCS siting in the US smoke literature.

PAPERS.title: Association of Urban Greenness and Air Pollution on Asthma Visits Among Children and Adolescents in Industrial and Non-Industrial Cities in Taiwan
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates an analysis of greenness and air pollution with paediatric asthma visits contrasting industrial and non-industrial Taiwanese cities. Recorded for coverage. Relevance: low-moderate.

PAPERS.title: Levels and contributing sources to PM2.5-bound PCDD/Fs and dl-PCBs in ambient air of Hanoi
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates measurement and source attribution of particle-bound dioxins, furans and dl-PCBs in Hanoi PM2.5. Recorded for coverage. Relevance: low - trace organics require filter sampling.

PAPERS.title: A unified framework for global indoor air quality: transitioning from guidelines to actionable open regulatory standards
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates a proposal to move indoor air quality from guideline values to open, enforceable standards. Recorded for coverage. Relevance: moderate - enforceable indoor standards would make low-cost indoor PM monitors compliance instruments, with the performance-certification burden that implies.
